# Independent audit of the arbitrary-multiplier sharp source cost

Audited `candidate 61e9db32fbeb3f83` in full.
The fixed-mass scalar reduction, its sharp realization, the exact global
optimizer, both asymptotics, and the Fenchel comparison all pass. No
mathematical correction was needed.

## Fixed mass, attainment, and realizability

Here the density is `rho=1_B+k eta`, but the source cost is
`v=(|B cap H|+eta(H))/|B|`. These distinct coefficients are retained
throughout the note. Its stated range is `d>=1`, real `k>=2`, and
`0<=eta<=1_B dx`.

The pushforward of uniform volume by its own upper-tail rank is uniform,
including for arbitrary convex bodies: scalar projections have no atoms
and their distribution is strictly monotone in the interior of the
projection. The domination of eta passes to this rank variable. The two
bathtub intervals consequently give the stated necessary inequality with
exact coefficients. At a scalar minimizer, decreasing both `s,r` keeps
`s+alpha-r` fixed; if `r=0`, decreasing only `s` preserves the remaining
constraints. Thus strict slack cannot persist at a minimum. The proof
also excludes both `s=0` and `s=1`, so no missing endpoint replaces the
claimed equality configuration.

For the one-variable root formulation, put `p=1/d` and
`c=alpha-r>=0`. Its slack derivative is

    q p(1+k alpha)s^(p-1)
       -k q[(s+c)^p-s^p]
       >=q p(1+k r)s^(p-1)>0.

The inequality is exactly the concavity bound for `x^p`; it includes
`d=1`, where that function is linear. The slack tends to a negative
limit at zero and grows to infinity, so the positive root is unique.
Clipping that root to `s>=r` and checking `s<=1-alpha+r` gives exactly
the original feasible set. The simplex realization makes the tail root
affine and hence makes Jensen equality exact. Its barycentric symmetry
also gives an actual full centroid, rather than merely a selected scalar
mean. Closed boundaries have zero volume and eta measure.

## Exact minimization over the added mass

The alpha derivative of the slack is nonpositive at fixed `s,r`, so
replacing alpha by r preserves feasibility. This operation leaves the
ABSOLUTE source cost `s+r` unchanged. The note correctly does not apply
it to the normalized objective `(s+r)/(1+alpha)`.

Independently setting `u=(r/s)^(1/d)` and `t=s^(1/d)` gives

    q t+k u^d(q-u)t^(d+1)=1.

For every `u in [0,1]` its unique root is at most `1/q<1`, and the
source cost increases with t. Hence minimizing over this compact u
interval loses no feasibility boundary. For `0<u<1`, differentiation
gives exactly the sign `1-k Z(u)t^d`. For `Z>0`, comparison at
`t0=(k Z)^(-1/d)` gives the sign change at `k=K(u)` with the orientation
printed in the note.

The independent expansion

    D(1+u^(d-1))-Z(1+u^d)
      =(1-u)[1+u^d+u^(d-1)(1+d(1-u))]

is positive. Thus K increases strictly from `1/(d gamma)` to infinity.
The exact threshold, the unique positive optimizer above it, and the
endpoint optimizer at zero all follow globally, rather than just from
a stationary equation. In particular the derivative may vanish at zero
when `d>1`; the interior sign calculation is still sufficient. The
separate `d=1` formula agrees with the independently proved interval
answer, including `k=2` and zero added mass.

An exact rational cross-check in dimension two is

    u=1/3, Z=11/9, D=53/27, k=2809/1331,
    s=1089/2809, r=alpha=121/2809,
    Xi=1210/2809.

Here `k>2`, `q=3/2`, `sqrt(s)=33/53`, and `sqrt(r)=11/53`.
Substitution verifies both the equality constraint and `k Z s=1`
using rational arithmetic. A triangle with eta on its vertex cap of
relative area r attains this value exactly. This check supplements the
general proof; it is not used in place of it.

## Fixed-d asymptotics and the normalized problem

The maximum of `(qE-E^q)/(1+E)^q` has derivative sign
`1-E^(1/d)-E/d`. There is one zero in `(0,1)`, matching `E_*=u_*^d`.
The lower and upper scalar roots in (11) sandwich Xi and, after
multiplication by `k^(d/(d+1))`, have the same positive limit. Thus the
printed sharp constant and power are exact for each fixed dimension.
No interchange of a dimension limit with the multiplier limit occurs.

For the normalized problem, the independent comparison

    v>=gamma(alpha+1/k)

implies `1+alpha<=1-1/k+v/gamma`. The latter denominator is positive,
and `v/(1-1/k+v/gamma)` is increasing for `k>1`. This proves both
inequalities in (12) without reducing alpha to r in the normalized
optimization. The exact absolute extremizers have `alpha=r<=Xi->0`,
so their normalized values have the same leading constant. Both sides
of the normalized asymptotic are therefore justified.

## Fenchel coefficients, endpoints, and scope

Dividing the fixed-alpha condition by `q s^q` gives exactly
`phi(U)+k phi(Q)+k phi(E)>=k/(d+1)`. Applying the three printed
Fenchel parameters and collecting their linear terms gives
`U+kQ-k(G-1)E<=k(G+1)` under (15). The final identity
`(1+k alpha)/s=U+kQ+kE-k` then gives the claimed source-cost bound.
The direct checks in dimensions one and two, and the elementary
binomial/exponential estimates for every `d>=3`, have the correct
constants and strictness. The independent one-band bathtub estimate
also gives (16), since `r>=s+alpha-1` and `s>=L`.

The result concerns one dominated measure eta with arbitrary density
coefficient k. It does not concern replacing eta by a sum of independently
dominated measures while changing the source numerator. The final
conditional transport interpretation correctly requires disjoint
original source budgets and one common dominated average measure. No
such decomposition of a general mixed-integer convex body is supplied
or presumed. In particular this theorem and its exact simplex examples
neither prove nor contradict the full mixed-integer conjecture.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
